title: SA/57/2012 of MOHAN SINGH AND ANOTHER Vs SMT. HEMA DEVI AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Second Appeal No. 57 of 2012
Mohan Singh and another ....... Appellants
 versus
Smt. Hema Devi & others ....... Respondents
Mr. Bhuwan Bhatt, Advocate holding brief of Mr. R.C. Upadhyay,
Advocate present for the appellants.
None is present for the respondents, despite service of notices upon them.
U.C. Dhyani, J.(Oral)

Present second appeal has been filed by the
plaintiffs / appellants being aggrieved against the judgment
and decree dated 16.03.2012, passed by learned District
Judge, Almora, in civil appeal no. 06 of 2008, titled as
Girish Chandra Bhandari and others vs Mohan Singh and
others.
2) A civil suit, being O.S. no. 02 of 2000, was
filed by the plaintiffs (appellants herein) against one Girish
Chandra Bhandari for permanent prohibitory injunction
directing the defendant not to interfere in the property in
question. The said suit was decreed by learned Civil Judge
(Jr. Div.), Ranikhet, vide judgment and decree dated
09.05.2008. Aggrieved against the same, the defendant
(since deceased) through his legal representatives Smt.
Hema Devi and others (respondents herein) filed a civil
appeal before the District Judge, Almora. The civil appeal,
being no. 06 of 2008, was allowed with costs and judgment
and decree under appeal was set aside, vide judgment and
decree dated 16.03.2012, passed by learned District Judge,

2
Almora. Aggrieved against the said judgment and decree,
present second appeal has been preferred by the plaintiffs
(appellants herein).
3) The second appeal was admitted by this Court
on 21.06.2012, on the following substantial question of
law:
 "Whether the appellate court is justified in
dismissing the suit on the ground that the report of
Advocate Commissioner has not been proved by the
plaintiff?
4) Plaint case, in brief, is that the parties are co-villagers. Plaintiff is the owner in possession of land
situated in khata khatauni no. 53. Plaintiff set up a kiosk on
plot no. 588 of khata khatauni no. 53 and was, accordingly,
earning his livelihood. Subsequent thereto, he was not
keeping well and, therefore, he hired the said kiosk (shop)
to the defendant on rent. The defendant raised pucca
construction on the same. Plaintiff instituted a suit for
permanent prohibitory injunction. Defendant assured the
plaintiff that he will not raise any construction on the same
and, therefore, the plaintiff withdrew his suit. Further, on
30.01.2000, the defendant again tried to raise construction
on the same and, therefore, the plaintiff had no option but
to file a suit for permanent prohibitory injunction. The
defendant, by filing the written statement, denied most of
the averments of the plaint. Defendant alleged that the
plaintiff, it appears, wants to encroach upon the kiosk of the
defendant. Defendant is the owner in possession of the suit
property in O.S. no. 08 of 1998, Advocate Commission

3
gave a report that there was no construction on plot no.
588. The earlier suit was dismissed by the trial court and,
therefore, the plaintiff was barred from filing a civil suit for
the same relief.
5) The trial court famed following issues on the
basis of pleadings of the parties:
 i) Whether the disputed property is part of plot no.
588 situated in khata khatauni no. 53? If so, its
effect?
 ii) Whether the plaintiff has any cause of action to
institute the suit?
 iii) To what relief, if any, is the plaintiff entitled?
 iv) Whether the suit is barred by the principle of res
judicata, as has been alleged by the defendant in
para 15 of his written statement.
6) Parties filed documentary evidence(s) in
support of their respective cases. Plaintiff examined
himself as PW1 and Bhupal as PW2. Defendant Ganesh
Chandra Bhandari examined himself as DW1, Har Singh as
DW2 and Dan Singh as DW3. The trial court, after
considering the evidence on record, came to the conclusion
that the plaintiff is the joint owner in possession of plot no.
588, khata khatauni no. 53. Plaintiff has raised a kiosk in
the said property. The defendant has no concern with the
same. The trial court has arrived to the said conclusion on
the report of Survey Commissioners as well as Advocate
Commissioner, apart from others. The trial court also came
to the conclusion that the defendant was tenant of the
plaintiff in the said kiosk.

4
7) So far as the issue on cause of action was
concerned, the trial court came to a definite finding that on
30.01.2000, defendant tried to encroach upon the property
of the plaintiff and, therefore, he had cause of action to
institute the suit.
8) The trial court also held that since the earlier
suit was withdrawn by the plaintiff (with liberty to file
fresh one), therefore, the suit was not barred by principle of
res judicata. Since the plaintiff was found to be owner in
possession of the plot no. 588 (khata khatauni no. 53),
therefore, the suit of the plaintiff was decreed. The
defendant was directed not to interfere with the said
property, vide judgment and decree dated 09.05.2008.
9) On appeal being preferred, learned lower
appellate court allowed the appeal with costs. Judgment
and decree passed by the trial court was set aside (vide
judgment and decree dated 16.07.2013, passed by learned
District Judge, Almora).
10) Learned lower appellate court came to the
following conclusions:
(A) No evidence has been offered by the plaintiff to
show that he let out the kiosk to the defendant.
PW1 stated, in his affidavit, that he is the owner of
plot no. 588. The father constructed the kiosk in
the year 1997-98 and after sometime, the kiosk
was let out to the defendant, but no date of letting
out or any receipt of running the shop by his father
has been filed by the plaintiff. In his cross-

5
examination, PW1 stated that he had no knowledge
whether any receipt of kiosk was issued by the
District Board or whether there was any license
obtained by his father to run the kiosk. PW1 was
also not aware as to whether any tax was paid by
the defendant to the District Board. PW1 also
admitted that he did not file any suit for
dispossession and recovery of rent from the
defendant. The evidence thus offered by the
plaintiffs does not establish that they have
constructed the kiosk in the year 1997-98 or they
ran any business from that kiosk. No rent has been
shown to be demanded by the plaintiff. No
possession has been sought by the plaintiff for the
said kiosk.
 (B) PW2, although stated in his examination-in-chief
that the kiosk was constructed in the year 1997, but
admitted in the cross-examination that defendant
Girish Chandra was running his shop at that kiosk.
PW2 did not know as to who constructed the
kiosk? In para 9 of his affidavit, PW2 stated that
he took the electricity connection in his own name.
He paid the tax to the District Board in his own
name. PW2 filed the document of electricity
connection and receipts of District Board before
the trial court. Defendant has duly supported his
case with the help of documents.
 (C) The argument of the plaintiff that defendant has
not called the Survey Commissioner for cross-examination has been negated by the lower
appellate court. The Commissioner's report was
confirmed on 11.10.2004, subject to the evidence
to be led by the parties.

6
 (D) Plaintiff is not in possession of the property in
dispute and, therefore, he was not entitled to get
the relief of permanent prohibitory injunction.

(11) The lower appellate court has dismissed the suit
not only on the ground that the report of the Advocate
Commissioner has not been proved by the plaintiffs but
also on the other grounds, viz., that the plaintiffs have
failed to establish that they constructed the kiosk in the year
1997-98. The plaintiffs also failed to establish that they ran
any business from that kiosk. Defendants are in possession
of the said kiosk. No possession has been sought by the
plaintiffs on the same. Even no rent was ever demanded by
the plaintiffs. There was no evidence on record to show
that the plaintiff ever let out the disputed kiosk to the
defendant and, accordingly, it was held that the kiosk was
constructed by the defendant. The plaintiffs failed to
establish that the disputed kiosk was constructed in the year
1997.
12) Learned counsel for the plaintiffs / appellants
relied on the case law of Shruti Fruits Private Limited
Kashipur and another vs Smt. Surelya, reported in 2009 (2)
U.D. pg. 430. In this case law, there is nothing as to
whether the survey report can be read in evidence without
being confirmed or if the report is confirmed subject to
evidence, plaintiff is duty bound to prove the report or not.
Learned counsel also relied on the principle of law laid
down by Hon'ble High Court in Deonandan Rai (deceased)
by L.Rs. vs Mahant Rai, 1983 All.L.J. 618. In this
authority, there was a case of handwriting expert in which

7
report was against the defendant and he has not called the
expert for cross-examination. But in the present case,
commissioner's report was confirmed subject to evidence
and he was not asked to prove his report. Ruling of
Gajanand (deceased) By L.Rs. and others vs Bishwanath
Singh Yadav (deceased) by L.Rs., 1982 All.L.J. NOC pg 87
was also relied by learned counsel for the plaintiff /
appellant. Said ruling is not applicable in the present case,
because, in this case, the suit was for mandatory injunction
for removal of the said chabutra and to restore the land in
its original condition. But in the case in hand, possession is
not sought by the plaintiff and the ruling relied by the
learned counsel is not applicable to the present case.
Survey commissioner has not been examined by the parties.
Report was confirmed subject to evidence. But plaintiff
failed to prove the report, and, as such, the finding recorded
by learned Trial Court was found by learned lower
appellate court to be erroneous in law.
13) Admittedly, plaintiffs are not in possession of
the property in dispute. In Jemma vs Raghu, reported in
AIR 1977 Orissa 12, it was held as under:
"The trial court as also the lower appellate court, clearly
found that the plaintiff was not in possession on the date
of the suit. A plaintiff not in possession is certainly not
entitled to the relief of injunction without claiming
recovery of possession. A reference may be had to the
Full Bench decision in the case of Masjid Shahid Ganj vs
S.G.P. Committee, AIR 1938 Lah 369 (F.B.); Abdul Nabi
vs Bajan Sahib, AIR 1944 Mad 221 and Hasmat Hussain
vs Inayat Ullah, AIR 1958 All 706 in this regard. From

8
the said ruling, it is absolutely clear that if the plaintiff is
not in possession, he cannot get the relief of permanent
injunction.

14) Since the defendant is found to be in possession
of the kiosk, therefore, learned lower appellate court rightly
pointed out that the relief of permanent injunction
restraining the defendant cannot be granted without
obtaining the relief of possession. The findings recorded
by learned lower appellate court draws strength from
various decisions of Hon'ble superior courts, a reference of
which has already been given in the judgment of the lower
appellate court. This Court need not multiply the judicial
authorities on the point. The Advocate Commissioner's
report was affirmed subject to evidence and the defendant
has been able to establish that he was in possession of the
kiosk standing on the disputed land. The report of the
Advocate Commissioner was not independent of the
evidence of the parties, for his report was confirmed subject
to evidence to be led by the parties. It will, therefore, be
wrong to argue that the lower appellate court dismissed the
suit only on the ground that the report of the Advocate
Commissioner was not proved by the plaintiff.
15) On the basis of the aforesaid discussion, the
substantial question of law is answered as follows:
 "Since there was no independent existence of the
report of the Advocate Commissioner, the same was
confirmed subject to evidence to be led by the parties,
and the defendant was able to establish that he was in
possession of the kiosk, which was constructed over the

9
disputed land, therefore, the lower appellate court was
justified in dismissing the suit on the ground that the
plaintiffs failed to establish their case and the Advocate
Commissioner gave its report in favour of the defendant."

16) No interference is called for in the judgment
and decree of lower appellate court, who has given cogent
reasons for allowing the first appeal and deciding the suit
against the plaintiffs, who were required to stand on their
own legs in order to succeed, in which they failed.
17) Second appeal, therefore fails and is dismissed.
No order as to costs.
